unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.

unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, provided paragraph (b) terms are met.

unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, when determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months following a break in service of seven years or more.

unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has had a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when an employee has a period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.statement: Section 825.110 does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Under 29 CFR 825.110 in relation to USERRA-covered service obligations.

unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including qualifying periods of paid or unpaid leave.

unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.
unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement following a continuous break in service of more than seven years.

unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
